summary: Part of Garphill Games' West Kingdom trilogy, Paladins has players recruiting workers to build city districts, defend against raiders, and spread faith, with a shared threat track that everyone contributes to and benefits from. It's a mid-heavy worker placement game with a satisfying tableau of building cards and dual-use resources.
praised: Great worker-placement puzzle with meaningful choices each turn
Attractive production and thematic building cards
criticised: Similar feel to its sister games (Architects, Viscounts) can feel repetitive if you own multiple
Some rules overhead with commissions and virtue track

interaction.kind: worker placement with a shared threat track
interaction.detail: Players place workers on shared action spaces, competing for limited slots, and everyone contributes to and draws from a communal 'outpost' track of raiders. Most building and scoring happens on individual player boards, so the interaction is indirect rather than confrontational.

scoring.how_you_win: Over a set number of rounds you place paladins to build outposts, recruit apprentices onto buildings, complete quests, and fend off raiders; whoever totals the most points from all these tracks plus leftover silver at game end wins.
